# Map

Builds a new array from the result of a lambda for each element of an array.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Map(items, callback)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to read, which is left unchanged. Null is read as the empty array; any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `callback` | function | A lambda of exactly one parameter, which receives the element; its result, of any type, null included, becomes the element of the new array at the same position. A lambda of any other number of parameters, or a value that is not a lambda, null included, is a runtime error. |

## Returns

Array. A new array of the lambda's results, one for each element of items, in the same order; the empty array when items is empty. Never null.

## Remarks

The lambda is called once for each element, in order. It is given the elements the array holds when the call starts, so a change the lambda makes to the array does not change which elements it is given.

## Example

`Map([1, 2, 3], x => x * 2)` returns `[2, 4, 6]`.
